name: Standing Quadriceps Stretch
summary: A standing static stretch targeting the anterior thigh and hip flexors by flexing one knee and drawing the heel toward the glutes.

setup: Stand upright with feet hip-width apart.
If needed for balance, place one hand lightly against a sturdy wall or chair.
steps: Shift your weight onto one supporting leg.
Bend the opposite knee and bring your heel toward your glutes.
Grasp your ankle or the top of your foot with the hand on the same side.
Align both knees next to each other and gently tuck your pelvis under to extend the hip.
Hold the stretch comfortably without arching your lower back, then slowly release and switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe slowly and evenly, deepening the stretch slightly on each exhalation.

common_faults.fault: Allowing the stretched knee to drift out to the side or forward.
common_faults.correction: Keep the thighs parallel and pointing directly toward the floor.

common_faults.fault: Hyperextending the lower back to pull the foot higher.
common_faults.correction: Keep your core engaged and maintain a neutral pelvis with a slight posterior tilt.

precautions: Avoid forcefully yanking on the ankle to prevent excessive stress on the knee joint.
